name: GT-R R35
summary: The 2025 Nissan GT-R R35 marks the final, highly refined iteration of the legendary platform, likely concluding with special T-spec and NISMO editions.

specs.label: Engine
specs.value: Hand-built 3.8-liter twin-turbo V6 (VR38DETT)

specs.label: Performance
specs.value: Premium Edition: 565 horsepower and 467 lb-ft of torque. NISMO/T-spec: 600 horsepower and 481 lb-ft of torque.

specs.label: Drivetrain
specs.value: ATTESA E-TS all-wheel-drive system with a 6-speed dual-clutch rear transaxle.

specs.label: 2025 Changes (JDM/T-spec)
specs.value: Introduction of new T-spec and Track Edition models with special NISMO-tuned suspension, carbon ceramic brakes, and enhanced, lighter engine components (piston rings, connecting rods).

specs.label: Exterior
specs.value: Updated aerodynamics, featuring a revised front bumper, grille, and a new, larger rear wing for the Nismo/T-spec variants.

specs.label: Interior
specs.value: Combination of Alcantara and leather, with special Blue Heaven interior color options for T-spec models.

name: CCGT
summary: The Koenigsegg CCGT was never meant to sit under showroom lights. Built as Koenigsegg's ambitious entry into GT1 racing and Le Mans, it was engineered to challenge the world's greatest race cars — before a sudden FIA regulation change ended its racing career before it ever competed. Only one prototype survives today, making it one of the rarest and most forgotten Koenigseggs ever created.

specs.label: Engine
specs.value: Naturally aspirated 5.0-litre V8 producing 600 horsepower — the maximum allowed under GT1 regulations.

specs.label: Drivetrain
specs.value: Rear-wheel drive via a 6-speed sequential magnesium transaxle gearbox, with straight-cut gears and dog-ring engagement.

specs.label: Chassis & Aero
specs.value: Carbon fibre semi-monocoque chassis weighing under 1,000 kg before mandatory ballast, generating over 600 kg of downforce. Race-spec pushrod suspension, carbon-ceramic brakes, centre-lock magnesium wheels.

specs.label: Legacy
specs.value: A one-of-one racing prototype born from Christian von Koenigsegg's dream of conquering Le Mans, remembered not for races won, but for what could have been.

name: Furai
price: Unobtainable (the only one built was destroyed)
summary: Unveiled in 2008, the Mazda Furai — Japanese for 'Sound of the Wind' — is one of the greatest automotive masterpieces that never made it to production, a machine sculpted almost entirely by aerodynamics. Developed with real track performance in mind, it blurred the line between race car and road-going fantasy with its screaming rotary soundtrack and futuristic bodywork.

specs.label: Chassis
specs.value: Built upon a Courage C65 Le Mans Prototype chassis.

specs.label: Engine
specs.value: Naturally aspirated 20B three-rotor rotary engine producing around 450 horsepower, designed to run on ethanol fuel.

specs.label: Weight
specs.value: Just 675 kg.

specs.label: Drivetrain
specs.value: Rear-wheel drive via a 6-speed sequential gearbox.

specs.label: Fate
specs.value: The one and only Furai was destroyed in a fire during a media test in 2008, leaving the world wondering what could have been.

name: Chiron Super Sport
summary: The Bugatti Chiron Super Sport represents the absolute peak of automotive engineering, a machine designed without compromise to push the boundaries of speed, luxury, and performance. Every curve of its elongated, aerodynamic 'longtail' body has been sculpted to optimize airflow and reduce drag, while carbon fibre construction keeps it both light and rigid.

specs.label: Engine
specs.value: 8.0-litre quad-turbocharged W16 producing 1,600 PS (1,578 hp) — a masterpiece of engineering that pulls relentlessly, even at extreme speed.

specs.label: Transmission
specs.value: 7-speed dual-clutch, shifting from 6th to 7th gear at 420 km/h under full load.

specs.label: Design
specs.value: A 'longtail' rear extends the body to hold laminar airflow longer, cutting aerodynamic stall by over 40%, while distinguishing it visually from the standard Chiron.

specs.label: Top Speed Note
specs.value: The standard production Super Sport is electronically limited to 440 km/h. Its limited-edition sibling, the 30-unit Chiron Super Sport 300+, had its limiter removed and set a record 490.484 km/h (304.773 mph) run in 2019 — the figure often quoted for this model.

name: Bolide
summary: The Bugatti Bolide is one of the most extreme track-focused machines ever created — a lightweight, uncompromising expression of Bugatti performance. Built around an ultra-rigid carbon fibre monocoque and developed with motorsport-grade aerodynamics, it strips away every road-car luxury in pursuit of raw speed, downforce, and lap-time capability.

specs.label: Engine
specs.value: 8.0-litre quad-turbocharged W16 producing 1,578 hp (1,600 PS) on standard pump fuel, or up to 1,825 hp (1,850 PS) on 110-octane racing fuel.

specs.label: Drivetrain
specs.value: 7-speed dual-clutch transmission driving all four wheels through an advanced all-wheel-drive system.

specs.label: Weight
specs.value: 1,240 kg dry — or 1,450 kg in FIA-compliant race trim — giving a power-to-weight ratio around 0.67-0.85 kg/hp, in Formula 1 territory.

specs.label: Aerodynamics
specs.value: Roughly 1,800 kg of downforce at 320 km/h thanks to an enormous rear wing, front splitter, underbody venturi tunnels, and an aggressive diffuser. Even the roof scoop uses an adaptive, morphable surface inspired by motorsport aero.

specs.label: Chassis & Brakes
specs.value: Race-style pushrod suspension, forged magnesium wheels with centre-lock hubs, and carbon-carbon racing brakes built for repeated high-speed track abuse.

specs.label: Cockpit
specs.value: A stripped, purposeful race interior: fixed-seat layout, six-point harnesses, FIA-style safety systems, a quick-release steering wheel, and digital race instrumentation. Non-road-legal, on full racing slicks.
